behavior: A freelancer can create a job: a quote with a payment schedule that the client accepts by link, which makes the deposit invoice
acceptance: POST /v1/profiles/{id}/jobs with an Idempotency-Key saves a job (title, scope, client name and email, 1-10 payments of title, USD amount with at most 2 decimals and days to pay; only the first may be on acceptance) with a link token and a copy of the issuer's billing details; the same request replays, another with the same key is 409; invalid input is 422; no billing details is 409 billing_details_required; another user is 403.

GET /v1/jobs/{token} is public and leaves out the client block; POST /v1/jobs/{token}/accept with a name and email records them and the time once, answers the same twice, and with a deposit makes exactly one invoice in the same transaction (payer chooses, the job title and client, one line for the payment, due the payment's days after the UTC day, checkout open 60 days past it); concurrent accepts make one invoice; an unknown token is 404 job_not_found.
GET /v1/profiles/{id}/jobs and /jobs/{jobId} list and read the owner's jobs with each payment's invoice id, number and status.
openapi.yaml, docs/backend/api.md and docs/backend/architecture.md describe the routes, rules and tables.
notes:
2026-10-18 review fail by reviewer: FAIL: one contract mismatch, plus three doc fixes to make in the same pass.

Blocking:
1. apps/backend/api/openapi.yaml:771 (GET /v1/jobs/{token}) and :786 (POST /v1/jobs/{token}/accept) have no `security: []`. The file's global security (line 11) asks for the Privy bearer token. So the spec says these routes need sign-in, but jobapi/routes.go:25-28 serves them in public. Every other public route has `security: []` (for example stopReminders at :630), and docs/backend/api.md (Auth) says public routes are marked that way.

Fix in the same pass (doc or contract accuracy):
2. Concurrent accepts across UTC midnight. job/accept.go:62 takes the due date from s.now(), and the invoice hash includes DueDate. Two clicks that land on both sides of 00:00 UTC get different hashes. The second one gets invoice.ErrConflict, wrapped at accept.go:52, so the client sees 409 idempotency_conflict. openapi does not list 409 for acceptJob. Data stays correct: the unique key still allows one invoice and one acceptance. Suggested fix: on invoice.ErrConflict, read ByToken again and return the job if it is accepted. Same day is proven by accept_test.go:96-133. Also docs/backend/api.md:308 says "That close is the same for every accept the same day". Only the offset (dueDays+61 days) and the due date are the same. The close time is the accept time plus that offset. Say that, and name the midnight case.
3. docs/backend/api.md:330 (Idempotency) says every POST that creates something needs an Idempotency-Key. The accept route creates an invoice without one. Add it to the exceptions: the link token and the key job:<jobId>:1 make it idempotent.
4. docs/backend/api.md:302 says the public read has no "ids". It returns payments[].invoiceId. Say "no job id or token".

Minor, not blocking:
- accept.go:52 adds "accept job <uuid>: " in front of invoice errors. httpio puts err.Error() into the 422 message, so a public client can see the internal job id and the owner's limit state (for example "a profile has at most 1000 receive addresses open at once", or no wallet).
- D-84 (sentences of at most 25 words): api.md:380-381 is 28 words; architecture.md:179-180's first sentence is 27.
- profiles_test.go round-robin is fine. The owner check is the same middleware on every route. Each of the 18 routes is checked once, and each of Alice's 4 profiles at least once. 18 x 4 calls would go over the 60 burst. Five {profileId} routes were already missing before this task and are still not listed: GET events, GET invoices/{invoiceId}, POST invoices/{invoiceId}/cancel, and GET and PUT notifications. Each has its own 403 test. But api.md:353 says every route is listed.
- jobs_test.go checks the unknown-token 404 only on GET, not on accept. Acceptance 3 says "list ... with each payment's invoice". The list returns counts (payments, paid); only the read returns each payment's invoice. That is fine if intended.
- The USD formatting is written twice: job/accept.go:61 and jobapi/model.go:95.
- httpio/errors.go:78 logs r.URL.Path on a 500, and that path includes the job link token. The reminder stop token already works this way.

For the later 10.3 tasks (not defects now):
- create.go:83-92 hashes json.Marshal(job.Request), which includes the shared profile.ClientDetails. Adding a field to either type changes every stored hash. invoice.requestHash uses a fixed format to avoid that.
- The key job:<id>:<position> cannot make a new invoice after that payment's invoice expires or is canceled.
- The position <= 10 CHECK and the single set of accepted_* columns mean a scope-change milestone that the client accepts (PLAN 10.3) needs a migration.
- The owner can use the key job:<id>:1 on invoice create first, which blocks acceptance. This only hurts the owner.
- MaxJobs 1000 counts every job ever made, and jobs cannot be deleted.

Checked and correct:
- Cents parsing: the regex, int64 range, and "300" equal to "300.00".
- The deposit invoice: payer chooses, USD with 2 decimals, and one line that sums exactly. The test checks 300000000 USDC base units.
- Due date and close: due is today UTC + dueDays, close is now + (dueDays+61) days, so the checkout stays open at least 60 days past the due date.
- After runs only inside the inserting transaction, never on a replay or on the unique-key race path.
- json:"-" is required: startRetainer marshals Request, and a func field would make that fail. cycle is not exported, so it is not marshaled.
- The job create race path checks the right constraint name (jobs_profile_id_idempotency_key_key).
- Locks: the profile row is locked first in both job create and accept, so there is no deadlock.
- Error mapping: 404 job_not_found, 409 idempotency_conflict and billing_details_required, 422 invalid_value.
- Model JSON matches openapi field for field.
- The public read leaves out client, acceptedEmail, jobId and token.
- Tokens are 32 random bytes.
- Rate limits and sweep follow the payer-email pattern.
- Nothing is emailed on accept.
- Layout and dependencies follow rules.md.
